answer: A forge is never so busy as the day the network turns work away. Once per epoch, without warning, the protocol doubles the fee on every signature for forty minutes - a brief gale through the canyon of traffic. Humans barely notice: they sign once or twice a day. Farms feel it across ten thousand accounts at once and must idle or bleed capital by the hour. Sybils optimize for steady cheapness; a mechanism that punishes bursts makes cheapness never quite steady.
